title: China is trying to regulate relationships with AI – can it work? | New Scientist
description: China is the first country to enact substantial legislation on AI relationships in an effort to protect people from the worst aspects of digital companions
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Magic rituals took place in an Australian cave for 25,000 years | New Scientist
description: Preserved plant cells show that grasses were brought into Cloggs cave in Australia and burnt over many millennia, revealing the ancient origins of rituals practised by the GunaiKurnai people
author: James Woodford

title: Effort to solve biggest controversy in mathematics has made no progress | New Scientist
description: For more than a decade, mathematicians have been unable to settle the question of whether the ABC conjecture has been solved. Fresh attempts to settle the debate are struggling to make headway
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Inhaling high-dose CO2 clears Alzheimer's proteins from the brain | New Scientist
description: Intermittently inhaling a high dose of carbon dioxide seems to remove the proteins amyloid and tau, which are implicated in Alzheimer's disease, from the brain by boosting its glymphatic system
author: Carissa Wong

title: AI's solution to 87-year-old riddle takes mathematicians by surprise | New Scientist
description: Mathematicians have been trying to prove the Jacobian conjecture for nearly a century, but now the Claude Fable 5 AI has apparently found a counterexample that disproves it
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Cloudy skies have slowed global warming – but that may be changing | New Scientist
description: Low cloud cover has been expanding since 1979, reflecting more sunlight into space, but scientists expect that trend to reverse and accelerate global warming
author: Alec Luhn
